Our approach

Working together

The scope depends on the problem. These are the things we agree along the way.

  1. 01

    Agree the focus

    Bring the context and the decision you need to make. Together, identify the questions, stakeholders and evidence that matter.

  2. 02

    Work through the evidence

    Map how the work happens, test the options with your team and make responsibilities clear.

  3. 03

    Leave a usable next step

    Translate decisions into practical actions, handovers and review points, with clear ownership.

Explore our approach +

Evidence first. Decision ready.

We name the owner, evidence, options, consequence and closure point. Then we translate the decision into implementable roles, artefacts, handoffs and readiness conditions, with measures and review points to keep the control working after implementation.

Discuss your operating model

From the working documents

The work, on the page.

Two extracts from the RSMS readiness study: a sample lifecycle and the decisions behind migration.

Selected diagram excerpts from the RSMS BAU readiness presentation, prepared by Dr. Ramzi Abbassi, April 2026. Examples of analysis and proposed controls.

The practice

Stay close to the work.

A small, senior-led practice working with the people who run the service. We trace the handovers, test the requirements and ask who can make the decision. The work needs to hold up when the project team leaves.

Explore the common challenges +

Process clarity

Map how work actually moves, expose manual handoffs and exceptions, and separate the designed pathway from the workaround.

Pattern resolution

Trace recurring symptoms to structural causes, so the organisation can address the control gap behind the issue.

Clear decision rights

Make ownership, evidence and decision pathways explicit, so control does not depend on individual memory.

Industry experience

Research systems. Regulated work. Operational handover.

Work that involves researchers, administrators, regulators and vendors, often with different requirements of the same system.

View sector experience +

Research and regulated systems: complex stakeholders, regulated samples, data standards, quality controls and platform adoption.

Vendors and procurement: requirements, RFQs, evaluation and the practical gap between vendor claims and implementable capability.

Operational transition: readiness, roles, training, support and transferable handover assets.
